best_for: Developers and testers who need to scan their own web apps for security holes without paying for a commercial scanner.

points.title: A proxy that attacks on request
points.text: ZAP sits between your browser and the site, so it can read and change every request. An automated scan crawls the app, checks pages passively, then runs real attacks against what it found.

points.title: Only scan what you may test
points.text: Active scans are real attacks and can damage data. The project says to use them only on apps you have permission to test. Safe mode limits the risk but also cuts much of what ZAP can do.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: ZAP is Apache-2.0 software with no paid tier. Extra checks and tools come from a community add-on marketplace inside the app.

points.title: Windows and Linux need Java
points.text: Windows and Linux builds need Java 17 or newer installed separately. The macOS downloads bundle Java 17, with separate Intel and Apple silicon builds.

points.title: Built for CI too
points.text: Docker images in stable, bare, weekly and nightly flavors let you run the same scans in a pipeline. Weekly builds come from the main branch, usually on Mondays.

points.title: Few old versions here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps only 3 versions, x64. macOS and Linux list only the current release. Linux comes as a Flathub build verified for the ZAP team, x64 only.
